solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Parent in employment? On the contrary — M

indicators.note: the clue first says the parent goes inside the employment, setting up a container
reverses the stated container order, so the employment word goes inside the parent word instead

parts.note: mum is an everyday word for a mother, a parent
use means employment, as in 'put to use'

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about a parent at work, broken off with a single letter.
explanation.walkthrough: M is this puzzle's theme abbreviation: each M clue is a London or Cambridge institution of this kind. 'On the contrary' flips 'Parent in employment' to employment in parent.
explanation.definitionFit: M is a standard abbreviation for this kind of institution, as on maps and in the puzzle's theme of famous collections.

clue.text: Army man moved to the Far East

indicators.note: the letters are shifted around into a new order

explanation.surface: A soldier being posted out to East Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the' is linking; the definition is a country standing for a place in the region.
explanation.definitionFit: The south-east Asian nation once called Burma lies in the region Europeans call the Orient.

clue.text: Proposer keeping marriage symbol from journalist

indicators.note: the proposer word holds the other inside it

parts.note: a suitor proposes marriage
the marriage bed stands for married life

explanation.surface: A man asking for a hand in marriage takes his token from a reporter.
explanation.definitionFit: A copy editor is a newspaper worker who checks and revises reporters' copy.

clue.text: Eradicate expert in outbuilding

indicators.note: the expert is placed inside the rearranged letters
the letters of out are built up anew in a fresh order

parts.note: a pro is a professional, an expert

explanation.surface: Get rid of a specialist living in a shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outbuilding' looks like a shed; it splits into 'out' and 'building', which makes UOT around PRO.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull something up by the roots is to eliminate it completely.

clue.text: Intermittently belonging to supporter fellow

parts.note: of expresses belonging, as in 'the house of my father'
a fan is a supporter of a team or star
a don is a fellow of a college at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: A college fellow is only now and then on the side of a supporter.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something that happens with gaps, starting and stopping, the same as occasionally or sporadically.

clue.text: M goes well, as they say, with leaving document to smallest hour

indicators.note: signals that the word is heard rather than read, so a sound-alike spelling is used

parts.note: fits means goes well, matches
a will is the document in which one leaves property
the first hour after midnight is 1 a.m., written with the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Something goes smoothly with a will made out in the small hours.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fitzwilliam is the great Cambridge institution in the M theme.
explanation.definitionFit: M abbreviates the kind of collection the Cambridge institution named after Viscount Fitzwilliam is.

clue.text: One who makes records shrink, say?

indicators.note: a spoken-word signal, so the word for shrink is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: shrink is slang for a psychiatrist or psychoanalyst

explanation.surface: Does a chronicler make psychiatrists of people?
explanation.definitionFit: A chronicler writes year-by-year historical accounts, keeping records.

clue.text: Mysterious Dickensian starting down with a cross?

indicators.note: takes the first letter of the next word

parts.note: a rood is a cross, especially a crucifix in a church

explanation.surface: A mysterious Dickens character setting off downhill carrying a crucifix.
explanation.walkthrough: Dickens's last, unfinished novel is The Mystery of Edwin Drood.
explanation.definitionFit: Edwin is the title figure of Dickens's unfinished mystery novel, hence a mysterious Dickensian.

clue.text: M's genuine past?

definitions.note: the possessive points to the subject a London institution of this kind is named after

parts.note: natural means genuine, unaffected
history is the past

explanation.surface: A question about whether an earlier life was authentic.
explanation.walkthrough: The South Kensington institution is the Natural History one.
explanation.definitionFit: M stands for the institution named after this field of study, the London collection of fossils and specimens.

clue.text: Second in warning of M with 18

indicators.note: the letter for second is placed inside the word for warning

parts.note: an alert is a warning
B stands for second, as a B grade or B-team is second-rate

explanation.surface: A runner-up sounds the alarm about something connected with a numbered clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 is VICTORIA; together with this answer it names the great South Kensington collection of art and design.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Consort's name joins his queen's in the title of the Victoria and Albert institution in London.

clue.text: Be prominent and plump outside

indicators.note: the word for plump sits around the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: stout means plump or portly
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone told to be noticeable and to look on the heavy side.
explanation.definitionFit: To be prominent is to be conspicuous, sticking out from the crowd, which this phrasal verb says.

clue.text: M in prelate about to go slow shortly

indicators.note: the prelate word goes around the other piece

parts.note: bish is a colloquial short form of bishop, a prelate
rit. is the short form of ritardando, the musical direction to slow down

explanation.surface: A bishop is about to dawdle a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link: the definition M sits in the clue before the wordplay. The British is the Bloomsbury institution in the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: The great Bloomsbury collection in London is the British one, so M stands for it.

clue.text: Most of see enters lake, which is not so good

indicators.note: one piece goes into the middle of the word for lake

parts.note: a mere is a lake, often in English place names

indicators.note: the word for see loses its last three letters, keeping the larger part

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese

explanation.surface: A bishop's territory floods into a lake, which is a poor outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: The ecclesiastical 'see' is the bishop's area, not the verb; DIOC is also its usual abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mediocre is only middling, of ordinary or second-rate quality rather than good.

clue.text: Girdle used by quiet flier

indicators.note: the letters of the garment's name are put to use in a different order

explanation.surface: A corset worn by someone flying silently.
explanation.definitionFit: An engineless aircraft rides air currents, so it flies without engine noise.

clue.text: M conned by superego?

indicators.note: the answer, given 'con' in front of it, makes the superego word, so those letters come off

parts.note: in Freud the superego is the part of the mind acting as conscience

explanation.surface: Someone tricked by their own moral self.
explanation.walkthrough: The South Kensington Science institution is the theme answer; prefixing CON to it makes the superego.
explanation.definitionFit: M stands for the London collection devoted to this field, near the other South Kensington ones.

clue.text: List of duties when climbing a hill

indicators.note: climbing goes upward, so in this clue the pieces are read from the end back

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A duty roster to consult when going up a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A roster sets out whose turn it is for each task, a schedule of duties.

clue.text: Immobile articles in shop next to checkout

indicators.note: the two pieces are placed side by side

parts.note: stocks are the goods a shop holds
a till is the cash register at a checkout

explanation.surface: Goods on the shelves beside the cash desk, standing motionless.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means perfectly still, not moving at all.

clue.text: Dish the flag when the south-west goes west?

parts.note: a flag is a kind of iris, the yellow flag of riverbanks

indicators.note: to go west is to be ruined, so these letters are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: Prepare a banner as the south-west region heads in the other direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes west' wants to mean a direction; it is the anagram signal, making HSTEW from THE and SW.
explanation.definitionFit: The mutton and potato casserole is a national dish of Ireland.

clue.text: Queen of M with 9

definitions.meaning: the British queen who reigned 1837 to 1901
the London institution named jointly for her and her consort, 9 across

explanation.definitionFit: The long-reigning queen's name begins the title of the South Kensington institution of art and design.

clue.text: I leave Kitchener or Profumo in Wiltshire

indicators.note: one letter departs from the longer phrase

parts.note: both held the British cabinet post of Secretary of State for War, so each was a war minister
taken as written

explanation.surface: A politician bows out of a role once held by famous British figures.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Kitchener (First World War) and John Profumo (1960s scandal) each held the British war ministry. The answer is a garrison town in Wiltshire, a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The market and army town sits in the west of the county of Wiltshire, England.

clue.text: See 5
Stresses hairstyle of stars?

definitions.meaning: a verb meaning emphasises or draws attention to
streaks of lighter colour in the hair, worn by celebrities

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition plays on stars both as celebrities and as lights high up in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: To emphasise a point is to pick it out, and dyed streaks pick out strands of hair.

clue.text: See 8
Patron of Scotland rewards devotees

annotationWithheld.why: Patron of Scotland rewards devotees: the answer is hidden in 'Scotland rewards', but 'Scotland' is also needed in the definition 'Patron of Scotland', and 'devotees' has no job; no blog parse found

clue.text: See 20
Bill for admission?

definitions.meaning: Bill is the first name of the Microsoft founder
the numbers of paying spectators admitted to a match, or the money they pay

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' is not an invoice but the forename of the Microsoft co-founder.
explanation.definitionFit: Attendance figures at matches, and the takings, are called by the same name as the entrances.

clue.text: A container like this is prickly

parts.note: a can is a metal container
thus means in this way, like this

explanation.surface: A tin of something that turns out to be spiky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prickly' stands for the prickly-leaved plant whose leaves inspired the Corinthian capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mediterranean plant has spiny, thistle-like leaves, a classic thorny garden perennial.

clue.text: Book that I received?

definitions.meaning: read as two words, a thing received was given to the speaker

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into two words: a gift you received was given to you.
explanation.definitionFit: A tome is a large and weighty volume.

clue.text: Crime not committed by short range phone

indicators.note: the letters are committed to a new order, as a crime is carried out

explanation.surface: An offence that was never carried out, investigated over an internal phone.
explanation.definitionFit: An internal communication system links rooms in one building, so it talks only over a short distance.

clue.text: Go round largely decayed fancy cave

indicators.note: the letters of go sit around the other piece

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: most of the word, dropping its last two letters

parts.note: rotten means decayed

explanation.surface: Travel around a mostly crumbling cavern decorated for show.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a feature is often an artificial cave, ornamented with shells in gardens of grand houses.

clue.text: Fool entertained by editor of periodical treated by hand

indicators.note: puts the editor piece beside the periodical
the fool is received inside the periodical, as a guest is entertained

parts.note: a mag is a magazine, a periodical
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A magazine's editor hosts an idiot, and some physiotherapy is done.
explanation.definitionFit: To knead and rub muscles is a therapy done with the hands.

clue.text: Great success in river like your average road system

indicators.note: the success word is placed within the river

parts.note: the Tay is the longest river in Scotland
a wow is a sensational hit

explanation.surface: A smash hit on a Scottish river, compared to ordinary traffic arrangements.
explanation.definitionFit: Most roads carry traffic in both directions, opposite flows sharing the carriageway.
